A Box Called Other
Level 5 · Advanced

Story + Workbook

Chapter 1

A tidy first assignment

1

Noor’s first assignment at the town office was to sort responses to a summerspace survey. The form offered three reasons for using the riverside square:
SHOPPING, RECREATION and OTHER. A neat chart would help councillors
decide where to spend a small improvement budget.
Noor liked the assignment. Unlike the arguments outside the meeting room,
a spreadsheet seemed to promise that every answer could find a place.
By midday, SHOPPING had a tall blue bar, RECREATION a shorter green one,
and OTHER an untidy collection of comments. The chart showed only the first
two. Its caption explained that miscellaneous responses had been excluded
for clarity.
Noor copied the caption without changing a word.
Read and circle
What reason does the caption give for leaving out the OTHER comments?
A. To protect the privacy of the people who replied
B. To keep the chart clear
C. Because the improvement budget was too small

2 · Think about it
What does the author signal by having Noor copy the caption without changing a
word?
A. She has not yet questioned the choice the caption hides
B. She has decided that every one of the OTHER comments is worthless
C. She has been ordered never to edit any caption

3 · Write it
Analyse the passive construction in the caption. Which decision-maker disappears,
and what reason is made to sound self-evident?
